sources.entry: dspy - A framework for programming, not prompting, language models.

summary.one_liner: DSPy is a Python framework for programming language models with compositional code instead of hand-written prompts, with optimizers that tune prompts and weights.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes DSPy as a framework for building modular AI systems, from simple classifiers to RAG pipelines and agent loops. It says the name stands for Declarative Self-improving Python and that users write Python code rather than brittle prompts. It offers algorithms for optimizing prompts and model weights. The LM integration is described as using bundled native lm15 engines, with no LiteLLM runtime dependency. The README itself is short and points to dspy.ai for full documentation. It also lists research papers behind the project, including GEPA, MIPRO-style instruction and demonstration optimization, and Demonstrate-Search-Predict.
use_cases: building modular LLM pipelines in Python
automatically optimizing prompts for a language model
fine-tuning model weights against a task metric
simple text classifiers driven by an LM
how_to_run: pip install git+ (install latest from main; URL is truncated in the README)
stack: language model providers via bundled lm15 engines
notable: Programs LMs with Python code instead of hand-written prompt strings
Includes optimizers that improve prompts and/or weights automatically
Covers classifiers, RAG pipelines, and agent loops with the same abstractions
Backed by published research papers such as GEPA and DSPy (ICLR 2024)
caveats: The README defers almost all usage detail to the external dspy.ai documentation site
Breaking changes to LM provider options, custom LMs, text completions, and embeddings are noted in a separate migration guide
The install-from-main command in the README is truncated and incomplete
